# OpenLit 0.1.0 candidate qualification

This is a private, unsigned candidate, not a published release. The package and
product are OpenLit; the command reports `lit 0.1.0`.

## Exact inputs

The five native archives were built from recovery source `53a23cc`, projected
into the private qualification repository as
`eb8eaec85328f8955998681d4cf72825afdbb2b0`. Only three unrelated workflows were
omitted; all other tracked files matched. The installer checks used source
`4d6a1db`, projection `9e9cdfbf44a589f53901e9bb275ea724b6301683`. No Rust source,
Cargo manifest, lockfile, license, or bundled notice changed between those sources.
Full IDs, hashes, test receipts, and raw-log hashes are in
[the machine-readable record](2026-11-20-openlit.json).

The original MIT LICENSE matches `98c59bb` byte for byte. Implementation used the
MIT recovery source and separately licensed dependencies. No post-MIT upstream
Lit source was consulted in this preparation. This statement does not extend the
scope of the earlier provenance audit or replace the pending transcript review.

## Results

- [Native archive run](https://github.com/mgkwill/lit-release-qualification/actions/runs/44814108615):
  five successful jobs, covering Linux x86-64/arm64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon,
  and Windows x86-64. Extracted archives passed identity, batch rollback, MCP,
  native/file/smart-HTTP remotes, and signature-vector checks. Unix jobs also
  checked documented examples. Windows strict sandbox launch was refused.
- Both Linux archives ran on Ubuntu 22.04 with glibc 2.35. Their highest required
  glibc symbol version is 2.34; older runtime support is not established.
- [Installer contract run](https://github.com/mgkwill/lit-release-qualification/actions/runs/44816029154):
  Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows passed. These checks use mock Cargo to verify the
  exact invocation, paths with spaces, failure propagation, and unchanged user
  settings. A real local macOS Cargo install also passed.
- The complete optimized Rust suite passed locally and on host-a, host-e, and
  host-f: 487 tests per platform, including the doctest. Formatting, clippy with
  warnings denied, and generated Rust documentation passed locally.
- Each lab host passed batch/MCP smoke, authenticated HTTPS/SSH Git remotes,
  and isolated-workspace tests against its source-built binary. Each also passed
  batch/MCP and authenticated-remotes tests against the downloaded Linux archive.
  Source-built and downloaded binary hashes are recorded separately.
- The sandbox's Actions-only ruleset and main commit were unchanged. The required
  `Agent workflow candidate` check remains bound to GitHub Actions integration
  15368; there are no bypass actors. No manual passing statuses were posted.

## Failures and limits

The ARM hosts could not start Bubblewrap's network setup: `RTM_NEWADDR` was denied.
Both refused strict-mode launch before running the payload, and the explicit
unavailable-backend tests passed. Successful ARM filesystem/network confinement
was **not** demonstrated in this run. host-a's positive confinement checks passed.
Host security policy was not relaxed to turn this into a passing positive test.

host-f initially lacked a runnable rustdoc. All compiled tests passed; the doctest
then passed using a matching Rust 1.99 rustdoc in a task-private directory. The
original failed command and successful retry are retained separately.

Two earlier Windows installer harness runs failed: one compared short and long
paths literally, and one treated a PowerShell-created AppData directory as a
file. The corrected harness preserves existing-file checks and rejects new Lit
configuration. The final three-platform run passed. A prior binary run was
canceled and replaced by the exact-source run above.

The dependency review removed ten of eleven vulnerability findings and four
unsoundness warnings. One AVX2 advisory remains reported; portable-only ML-DSA
mitigates it and passed the independently licensed verification vectors. Five
maintenance warnings remain. See [the dependency review](../../../docs/DEPENDENCIES.md).
The audit is not clean, and the notice inventory is not a completed license review.

## Custody and remaining gates

The five archives, checksum manifest, source ID, receipts, and raw logs are saved
outside Git under the original verification directory, in
`release-candidate-openlit-0.1.0-53a23cc/`. Their bytes and bundled notices were
checked again when copied. Checksums alone do not authenticate a publisher.

Publisher identity selection, platform signatures, notarization, Actions
attestations, final signed-byte tests, dependency-notice review, final provenance
review, and reviewed transcript archival remain open. Public tags, registry
publication, release publication, and repository renaming were not performed.
The owner must approve the exact release before any publication.
